subject: Biology
title: Plant Kingdom
summary: Plantae includes algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms. Classification moved from artificial systems (few morphological characters) to natural systems (many characters) to phylogenetic systems (evolutionary relationships).
Algae are simple, thalloid, mostly aquatic; they are grouped by pigments and stored food into green (Chlorophyceae), brown (Phaeophyceae) and red (Rhodophyceae) algae.

Bryophytes (amphibians of the plant kingdom) have a dominant gametophyte. Pteridophytes are the first vascular plants with a dominant sporophyte. Gymnosperms have naked seeds; angiosperms have seeds inside fruits.
Plant life cycles show alternation of generations — haplontic, diplontic or haplo-diplontic.

formulas.name: Algal classes
formulas.formula: Chlorophyceae: chlorophyll a, b; starch; cellulose wall (Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra, Chara);  Phaeophyceae: chlorophyll a, c, fucoxanthin; laminarin, mannitol; algin (Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum, Fucus);  Rhodophyceae: chlorophyll a, d, r-phycoerythrin; floridean starch (Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Gracilaria, Gelidium)

formulas.name: Algal reproduction
formulas.formula: isogamous (similar gametes — Ulothrix, Spirogyra);  anisogamous (dissimilar size — Eudorina);  oogamous (large egg + small sperm — Volvox, Fucus)

formulas.name: Useful algae
formulas.formula: agar (Gelidium, Gracilaria);  carrageen (red algae);  algin (brown algae);  Chlorella — protein-rich food supplement used by space travellers

formulas.name: Bryophytes
formulas.formula: gametophyte dominant; rhizoids; sporophyte (foot, seta, capsule) depends on gametophyte; water needed for fertilisation
formulas.note: Sphagnum gives peat, used as fuel and as packing material because it holds water.

formulas.name: Moss life cycle
formulas.formula: spore → protonema (creeping, green, filamentous) → leafy stage (bears sex organs) → zygote → sporophyte

formulas.name: Bryophyte life cycle (order)
formulas.formula: haploid gametophyte attached to the substratum by rhizoids → antheridia release antherozoids into water → antherozoid fuses with the egg in the archegonium → zygote (no meiosis yet) → multicellular sporophyte (foot, seta, capsule) → meiosis (reduction division) in the capsule → haploid spores → new gametophyte

formulas.name: Pteridophytes
formulas.formula: sporophyte dominant with true roots, stems, leaves and vascular tissue; spores in sporangia on sporophylls; gametophyte = prothallus; water needed for fertilisation

formulas.name: Pteridophyte life cycle (order)
formulas.formula: sporophyte (2n) → sporangia on sporophylls → meiosis in spore mother cells → haploid spores → spore germinates into the prothallus (small, free-living, mostly photosynthetic gametophyte of cool, damp, shady places) → antheridia and archegonia form on it → antherozoids reach the archegonia through water → fertilisation → zygote → new sporophyte

formulas.name: Heterospory
formulas.formula: megaspores (female gametophyte) + microspores (male gametophyte) — Selaginella, Salvinia
formulas.when: A step towards the seed habit.

formulas.name: Pteridophyte classes
formulas.formula: Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum), Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum)

formulas.name: Gymnosperms
formulas.formula: ovules not enclosed (naked seeds); microsporophylls and megasporophylls in cones (strobili); pollen grains carried by wind; no water needed for fertilisation
formulas.note: Coralloid roots of Cycas have N₂-fixing cyanobacteria; Pinus roots have mycorrhiza.

formulas.name: Angiosperm double fertilisation
formulas.formula: male gamete 1 + egg → zygote (2n);  male gamete 2 + secondary nucleus (2 polar nuclei) → primary endosperm nucleus (3n)

formulas.name: Ploidy in seeds
formulas.formula: gymnosperm endosperm = n (female gametophyte);  angiosperm endosperm = 3n

formulas.name: Life cycle patterns
formulas.formula: haplontic: dominant gametophyte, zygote only diploid stage (Volvox, Spirogyra, Chlamydomonas);  diplontic: dominant sporophyte, gametes only haploid stage (seed plants, Fucus);  haplo-diplontic: both multicellular (bryophytes, pteridophytes; Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia, kelps)

examples.title: Amphibians of plants
examples.problem: Why are bryophytes called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?
examples.solution: They live on land but need water for sexual reproduction (sperm swim to the egg).

examples.title: First vascular plants
examples.problem: Which group first had xylem and phloem, and which generation is dominant there?
examples.solution: Pteridophytes; the sporophyte is the dominant, independent generation.

examples.title: Ploidy count
examples.problem: In a moss, state the ploidy of protonema, leafy stage, capsule and spores.
examples.solution: Protonema n, leafy stage n, capsule (sporophyte) 2n, spores n (formed by meiosis).

examples.title: Life cycle type
examples.solution: Diplontic — the sporophyte is dominant and the gametes are the only haploid stage.

examples.title: Agar source
examples.problem: Agar used in microbiology comes from which algae?

examples.title: Giant trees
examples.solution: Sequoia (giant redwood) — one of the tallest tree species.

topics.title: Systems of classification
topics.explain: Artificial (Linnaeus; mainly vegetative characters or androecium), natural (Bentham and Hooker; internal and external features) and phylogenetic (evolutionary). Numerical taxonomy uses computers and gives equal weight to all characters; cytotaxonomy uses chromosome number and structure; chemotaxonomy uses chemical constituents.

topics.title: Algae general features
topics.explain: Chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic, largely aquatic. Forms range from unicellular (Chlamydomonas) and colonial (Volvox) to filamentous (Ulothrix, Spirogyra) and large marine kelps. They fix about half of all CO₂ on Earth.

topics.title: Liverworts
topics.explain: Thalloid (Marchantia), dorsiventral. Asexual reproduction by fragmentation and gemmae (green, multicellular buds in gemma cups). Sporophyte has foot, seta and capsule.

topics.title: Gymnosperm details
topics.explain: Roots are generally tap roots; stems can be unbranched (Cycas) or branched (Pinus); leaves are needle-like in conifers (thick cuticle, sunken stomata reduce water loss). Male cone has microsporophylls; female cone has megasporophylls with ovules; the female gametophyte has archegonia.

topics.title: Angiosperms
topics.explain: Flowering plants: dicots and monocots. Size ranges from tiny Wolffia to tall Eucalyptus (over 100 m). Flower has stamens (anthers → pollen) and pistil (ovary with ovules); the embryo sac has 7 cells and 8 nuclei.

topics.title: Ecological importance
topics.explain: Bryophytes and lichens are pioneers on rocks and help form soil; mosses prevent soil erosion. Pteridophytes are used medicinally and as soil binders and ornamentals.

ratta: Green: a, b, starch;  brown: a, c, fucoxanthin, laminarin;  red: a, d, phycoerythrin, floridean starch.
Bryophyte: gametophyte dominant;  pteridophyte onwards: sporophyte dominant.
Haplontic: Volvox, Spirogyra;  diplontic: seed plants, Fucus;  haplo-diplontic: bryophytes, pteridophytes, Ectocarpus.
Agar: Gelidium, Gracilaria;  Chlorella for space travellers.
Bryophyte order: rhizoids attach → antherozoids in water → fertilisation → sporophyte → meiosis → spores.
Pteridophyte order: meiosis in spore mother cells → spores → prothallus → antheridia/archegonia → water → fertilisation.
